Communicating Sequential Processes (Hoare), The Next 700 Programming Languages (Landin), As We May Think (Bush), Can Programming Be Liberated from the von Neumann Style (Backus)

And this seems to be a cool course: [course] > This course examines papers every computer scientist should have read, from the 1930s to the present. It is meant to be a synthesizing experience for advanced students in computer science: a way for them to see the field as a whole, not through a survey, but by reliving the experience of its creation. The idea is to create a unified view of the field of computer science, for students who already know something about it, by replaying its entire evolution at an…
